terms.gloss: a leaf; of a flower, a petal
evidence: Plin. NH 21.16: differunt enim multitūdine foliōrum (of roses)
terms.comment: Latin has no separate word: Pliny counts the “leaves” of the rose, and calls the many-petalled kind centifolia, hundred-leaved (NH 21.17).

From the Greek for a leaf or a thin plate. In Isidore and the medieval dictionaries it is a plate of metal; of a flower it is first found in the seventeenth century (Morgan–Owens, from the Oxford English Dictionary).

phrases.latin: differunt enim multitūdine foliōrum, asperitāte, lēvōre, colōre, odōre
phrases.english: for they (the kinds of rose) differ in the number of their petals, in roughness, smoothness, colour, and scent
the fewest petals (a rose has) are five

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. petal.
